# Sirach 16 — Disagreement Log

**Date:** 2026-03-17
**Chapter:** Sirach 16 (30 verses)
**Total Disagreements:** 17

---

## Disagreement 1 — Verse 3

**Issue:** "To die childless" vs. "to die without children"
- EMET: "to die childless"
- LOGOS: "to die without children"
- PNEUMA: "to die without children"
- SOPHIA: "to die without children"

**Resolution:** Both acceptable. "Without children" slightly more transparent. SOPHIA adopted.

---

## Disagreement 2 — Verse 4

**Issue:** "Populate a city" vs. "repopulate a city"
- EMET: "will populate a city"
- LOGOS: "may be repopulated"
- PNEUMA: "can repopulate a whole city"
- SOPHIA: "may be repopulated"

**Resolution:** Context suggests rebuilding a depleted city. "Repopulate" (LOGOS/PNEUMA/SOPHIA) better captures this. SOPHIA adopted.

---

## Disagreement 3 — Verse 6

**Issue:** "Wrath is kindled" vs. "wrath is ignited"
- EMET: "wrath is kindled"
- LOGOS: "wrath is ignited"
- PNEUMA: "God's anger ignites"
- SOPHIA: "wrath is ignited"

**Resolution:** PNEUMA adds "God's" as subject where original leaves it implicit. LOGOS/SOPHIA "ignited" is equivalent to EMET "kindled." SOPHIA adopted.

---

## Disagreement 4 — Verse 7

**Issue:** "Ancient giants" — the Nephilim reference
- EMET: "the ancient giants who revolted in their strength"
- LOGOS: "the ancient giants who rebelled in their great strength"
- PNEUMA: "the ancient giants who rose up in their great strength"
- SOPHIA: "the ancient giants who rebelled in their strength"

**Resolution:** Greek ἀρχαῖοι γίγαντες = ancient/primeval giants. Reference to Gen 6:1-4 and 1 Enoch tradition. All agents retain "giants." "Rebelled" (LOGOS/SOPHIA) is more precise than "revolted." SOPHIA adopted.

---

## Disagreement 5 — Verse 9

**Issue:** "Nation doomed to destruction" vs. "nation devoted to destruction"
- EMET: "the nation doomed to destruction"
- LOGOS: "the nation devoted to destruction"
- PNEUMA: "the people marked for destruction"
- SOPHIA: "the nation devoted to destruction"

**Resolution:** Greek κατεσκαμμένη = those who were marked out/devoted for destruction. This refers to Canaanites under herem. "Devoted" (LOGOS/SOPHIA) carries the herem theological sense. SOPHIA adopted.

---

## Disagreement 6 — Verse 10

**Issue:** "Six hundred thousand infantry" — the Exodus reference
- EMET: "six hundred thousand infantry"
- LOGOS: "six hundred thousand foot soldiers"
- PNEUMA: "six hundred thousand foot soldiers"
- SOPHIA: "six hundred thousand foot soldiers"

**Resolution:** Greek πεζοί = foot soldiers. LOGOS/PNEUMA/SOPHIA "foot soldiers" more specific than "infantry" (implying organized military). SOPHIA adopted.

---

## Disagreement 7 — Verse 10b

**Issue:** "Hardness of their hearts" vs. "stubbornness of their hearts"
- EMET: "hardness of their hearts"
- LOGOS: "stubbornness of their hearts"
- PNEUMA: "hardened their hearts"
- SOPHIA: "stubbornness of their hearts"

**Resolution:** Greek σκληροκαρδία = hard-heartedness. Both "hardness" and "stubbornness" valid. LOGOS/SOPHIA "stubbornness" is more idiomatic. SOPHIA adopted.

---

## Disagreement 8 — Verse 11

**Issue:** "Pours out wrath" — active vs. passive
- EMET: "to pour out wrath"
- LOGOS: "he pours out wrath"
- PNEUMA: "the power to judge"
- SOPHIA: "he pours out wrath"

**Resolution:** PNEUMA changes "pour out wrath" to "power to judge" — loses the image. LOGOS/SOPHIA retain the verb. SOPHIA adopted.

---

## Disagreement 9 — Verse 13

**Issue:** "Will not be frustrated" vs. "will not be cut short"
- EMET: "the patience of the devout will not be frustrated"
- LOGOS: "the patience of the devout will not be cut short"
- PNEUMA: "the patient endurance of the faithful won't be in vain"
- SOPHIA: "the patience of the devout will not be cut short"

**Resolution:** Greek οὐ κολοβωθήσεται = will not be cut short/curtailed. LOGOS/SOPHIA "cut short" most literal. SOPHIA adopted.

---

## Disagreement 10 — Verse 15

**Issue:** Pharaoh passage — inclusion/exclusion in Vaticanus
- EMET: "He hardened Pharaoh so that he did not acknowledge him"
- LOGOS: "He hardened Pharaoh so that he would not acknowledge him"
- PNEUMA: same meaning
- SOPHIA: "He hardened Pharaoh so that he would not acknowledge him"

**Resolution:** This verse exists in some manuscripts. All agents include it. Minor variation in "did not" vs. "would not" — LOGOS/SOPHIA use subjunctive ("would not") appropriately for purpose clause. SOPHIA adopted.

---

## Disagreement 11 — Verse 17

**Issue:** The soliloquy of the person hiding from God
- EMET: "for what is my soul among the immense creation"
- LOGOS: "for what am I among so vast a creation"
- PNEUMA: "just one tiny soul in a vast creation"
- SOPHIA: "for what is my soul amid so vast a creation"

**Resolution:** EMET retains "soul" (psyche). LOGOS loses "soul." PNEUMA adds "tiny." SOPHIA retains "soul" with LOGOS' "vast creation." SOPHIA adopted.

---

## Disagreement 12 — Verse 18

**Issue:** "Heaven of heavens" — the cosmological phrase
- EMET: "the heaven and the heaven of heavens"
- LOGOS: "heaven and the highest heaven"
- PNEUMA: "the heavens and the highest heavens"
- SOPHIA: "the heaven and the heaven of heavens"

**Resolution:** Greek ὁ οὐρανὸς καὶ ὁ οὐρανὸς τοῦ οὐρανοῦ = heaven and the heaven of heaven. The literal is deliberately cosmological. EMET/SOPHIA retain the literal phrasing which echoes Deut 10:14, 1 Kings 8:27. SOPHIA adopted.

---

## Disagreement 13 — Verse 21

**Issue:** "Storm that no man can see" — the subject of seeing
- EMET: "a storm that no man can see"
- LOGOS: "a tempest that no human eye can see"
- PNEUMA: "a storm that comes and goes unseen"
- SOPHIA: "a storm that no eye can see"

**Resolution:** LOGOS "tempest" is slightly more intense than "storm." SOPHIA's "no eye can see" is compact. SOPHIA adopted.

---

## Disagreement 14 — Verse 22

**Issue:** "Acts of righteousness" vs. "deeds of justice"
- EMET: "his acts of righteousness"
- LOGOS: "his deeds of justice"
- PNEUMA: "all his righteous deeds"
- SOPHIA: "his deeds of justice"

**Resolution:** Greek δικαιοσύνη covers both righteousness and justice. LOGOS/SOPHIA "deeds of justice" has a more forensic edge appropriate to context. SOPHIA adopted.

---

## Disagreement 15 — Verse 22b

**Issue:** "The covenant is far away" vs. "the appointed time is far off"
- EMET: "the covenant is far away"
- LOGOS: "the decree is far off"
- PNEUMA: "the appointed time seems so far away"
- SOPHIA: "the appointed time is far off"

**Resolution:** Greek διαθήκη can = covenant or decree. EMET "covenant" is too specific without context. LOGOS "decree" and SOPHIA "appointed time" capture the sense of a future reckoning that seems distant. SOPHIA adopted.

---

## Disagreement 16 — Verse 27

**Issue:** "They do not cease from their work" vs. "they never cease from their work"
- EMET: "they do not cease from their work"
- LOGOS: "they do not rest from their labors"
- PNEUMA: "they never stop their work"
- SOPHIA: "they never cease from their work"

**Resolution:** LOGOS "rest from their labors" introduces the Sabbath rest theme which is not in the Greek. PNEUMA/SOPHIA closer to literal. SOPHIA adopted.

---

## Disagreement 17 — Verse 30

**Issue:** "Covered its surface" — what covers the earth
- EMET: "With all kinds of living things he covered its surface"
- LOGOS: "With every kind of living creature he covered its surface"
- PNEUMA: "He covered its surface with every kind of living creature"
- SOPHIA: "With all kinds of living creatures he covered its surface"

**Resolution:** Minor variation in word order and "things/creatures." "Creatures" (LOGOS/SOPHIA) more specific. SOPHIA adopted.
